_comment: The status checks the branch ruleset 'protect-main' requires on main, declared here so a
workflow change can be checked against them WITHOUT a network call. This file is a DECLARATION,
not the truth: the truth lives in the ruleset. scripts/required_check_reachability_gate.py
--verify-declaration compares the two and reports drift; the offline gate only asks whether the
workflows can produce what is declared.
Why this file exists: three times in this repository a required context could not be produced,
and every time a human reading found it, never a mechanism. See the class note below.
_class: A required status check has TWO failure modes, red and ABSENT, and only the first is visible.
An absent context produces no line, no colour and no message; the pull request simply stays
BLOCKED with nothing red on it. GitHub has no API field that separates 'still running' from
'will never be reported' (measured 2026-09-16; mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED covers both).
Known instances in this repository:
1. ci.yml lacked the 'labeled' trigger, so adding the landung label to a resting PR started
no run at all. Closed 2026-09-14 in commit 89301253.
2. fork-pr-isolation.yml lacked the 'merge_group' trigger. It is the SECOND of two files that
carry required contexts; the assumption had been that all seven lived in one file.
3. The test matrix produces five Python versions only under a condition, so four of the seven
required contexts are never created for an ordinary pull request. Measured 2026-09-16 on
PRs 209, 210, 211 and 212, all four BLOCKED with no required check red.
4. The reachability job itself. It judged the STRUCTURE (produced under a named condition,
accepted by the ratchet) and reported green on pull request 218 while the condition was
false on that event: no label, no release/ head, no dispatch. The four contexts were never
going to arrive and nothing on the pull request said so. Measured 2026-09-17. Closed the
same day by the live step (--live): the condition is evaluated against the run's own event.
5. The other half of the same class: a check that is PRODUCED but can never block. A job
with `needs` and no always()/!cancelled() guard is skipped whenever a needed job fails,
and GitHub counts a skipped required check as passed. The collector job all-checks-passed
(ci.yml, 2026-09-17) carries `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` for exactly that reason, and the
gate reports a required context on an unguarded needs-job as skipped-is-passed and exits 1.
A condition made only of always()/!cancelled() is read as unconditional, not as a gate.
_ratchet: accepted_gated names the contexts whose CONDITIONAL production is knowingly accepted today, and
binds each one to the sha256 of the exact condition that was accepted. A name alone is not
enough and is rejected as an unbound acceptance: a name that is once on the list would otherwise
be immune forever, so a context that runs unconditionally today and disappears behind an `if:`
tomorrow would slip through, and a condition could be narrowed at will while the name stayed put.
Two independent reviewers found that same hole on 2026-09-16, one of them by building the case
and measuring exit 0 on it.
Why the ratchet exists at all: an advisory job that is red from its very first run teaches people
to look away, and a gate that is habitually stepped over checks nothing any more.
The list is a RATCHET, not an exemption: the report still names every conditional context with
its condition and its digest. Only the exit code follows the ratchet.
It turns RED as soon as something gets WORSE: a context that is not produced at all, a dead
condition, something not measurable, a newly conditional context, or a changed condition.
accepted_unreadable works symmetrically, and since 2026-09-16 that is true of the BINDING too:
each entry names its context and the sha256 of the exact REASON it was accepted for. The
same job can be unmeasurable tomorrow for a DIFFERENT reason, and that reason is not
accepted. A third reviewer measured exactly that on 2026-09-16: same prefix, reason changed
from 'calls a reusable workflow' to 'matrix values not readable literally', exit 0, nothing
reported. A name-only entry is rejected as an unbound acceptance, like its gated sibling.
Without it the
gate would be red forever because of ONE permanent limit, which would move the permanent red
rather than remove it. A NEW unmeasurable case still fails -- and since 2026-09-16 it fails
even when every required context is produced unconditionally. That check used to sit BELOW
the shortcut for the all-produced verdict, so it only ever ran when something was already
conditional; measured while writing the case for the bound limit, the report printed the new
unmeasurable line and the gate still exited 0. An unmeasurable spot can hide a required
context, and that is true regardless of how the others stand.
KNOWN LIMIT of this file, named rather than hidden: the declaration is its own input.
Removing a context from a workflow AND from required_contexts in the same change is
invisible to the offline gate. Two reviewers named this the main weakness on 2026-09-16.
It is not left as prose: the ci.yml job now runs --verify-declaration against the live
ruleset BEFORE the offline gate, so a red offline result cannot skip it. That check needs
the network and a token; when it cannot run it reports not-measurable, never a pass.
accepted_gated_reason: These four are produced only when the full test matrix runs. Since 2026-09-17 (owner directive, velocity) that matrix runs for EVERY pull request from this repository; the shared five-branch condition is: a workflow_dispatch run, a pull request whose head repository is this repository, a ref name starting with release/, the 'landung' label, or a merge_group event. Only a FORK pull request without the label runs the fast layer. The acceptance binds to the sha256 of that condition, not to the context name, so narrowing the condition while keeping the name is a regression and turns the gate red. Stands until the owner decides on the aggregator job (card OA-3c67b06ad6).
accepted_unreadable_reason: A reusable workflow reports as '<caller job id> / <called job name>'. The gate deliberately does not derive that name instead of guessing it. This is a permanent limit of the design, not a regression.
